summary: Intermittent artifact integrity failures: corporate egress cache merging range requests corrupts presigned S3 downloads
description: Issue summary: Customer running Redwood Private (VPC peered) reports intermittent SHA256 mismatches when downloading model artifacts using presigned S3 URLs. Downloads sometimes succeed but more often the artifact file fails checksum validation during model load.
impact: Model loads failing on worker nodes for specific subnets; affects inference rollouts across a subset of on-prem edge appliances. Customer reports ~12% failed pulls over the last 12 hours for new container starts. Production traffic degraded for endpoints backed by the affected model; customer is on a private deployment with strict deployment windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a host in the customer's private subnet (same as agents experiencing failures), perform a presigned S3 GET for a model artifact URL generated by Redwood control plane.

2) Repeat the download multiple times using curl with range support (e.g., curl --range 0- -o artifact.part <presigned-url>), or use the platform's artifact fetcher which performs ranged GETs / parallel range merges.
3) Compute sha256sum of the downloaded file and compare against the expected checksum returned by control plane metadata.
4) Observe intermittent mismatches; sometimes a retry yields a correct checksum. Failures correlate to downloads initiated from a specific corporate egress appliance (customer-provided).
observed_logs: artifact-fetcher: completed range merge: segments [0-1048575],[1048576-2097151] -> write 2097152 bytes
kernel: TCP: duplicate ACKs seen during download from 10.12.5.1 (egress proxy)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: corruption at the gateway or middlebox that rewrites HTTP headers (Content-Length / Transfer-Encoding) when merging range requests.

Customer provided tcpdump from an affected host: pcap shows HTTP/1.1 responses from internal egress cache with 'Content-Range' responses that overlap and an extra CRLF injected between range segments.

We reproduced with a cURL loop via the customer's VPN and observed the egress cache (vendor: FastEdge 4.2) rewriting chunk boundaries and returning merged fragments without correct byte ordering in ~1/8 attempts.

Control plane logs show the presigned URL signed correctly and S3 responds with 206 Partial Content for range requests. The corruption appears after the egress appliance (responses from S3 are correct in packet captures taken from upstream of the appliance).

We checked signature/timestamp expiration edge cases — not applicable (URLs valid for >1h). TLS termination does not occur on the appliance (it acts as an L7 HTTP proxy) and performs reassembly of multi-part ranges.

This behavior is consistent with an egress cache attempting to be helpful by combining ranges for parallel downloads but doing so incorrectly for certain boundary alignments and when connection pooling is active.
customer_communications: 2026-03-11 09:15 UTC - Maya Chen: Opened ticket after customer reported artifact checksum mismatches during rollout.
2026-03-11 10:02 UTC - Diego Alvarez: Requested tcpdumps and vendor model/version of egress proxy; asked for sample presigned URL and expected checksum (customer provided via secure upload).
2026-03-11 12:45 UTC - NimbleRetail SRE (Jordan Mills): Provided tcpdump and egress proxy config (FastEdge v4.2, range-merge enabled, http-inspect enabled).
2026-03-12 03:10 UTC - Diego Alvarez: Shared reproduction steps and recommended temporary mitigations to avoid corruption during rollout (see resolution notes).
temporary_mitigation_and_resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC: Instructed customer to disable 'range-merge' / parallel-range coalescing on the FastEdge appliance for the affected subnets. After this change, artifact downloads succeed consistently and checksums validate in 100/100 subsequent attempts.
Workaround: Configure artifact fetcher to avoid parallel range downloads by setting REDWOOD_ARTIFACT_RANGE_PARALLEL=0 for the agent process, or ensure egress device does not perform range coalescing.

Permanent fix path: Customer to schedule firmware upgrade for FastEdge to v4.2.5 which vendor claims to fix range-merge ordering bug, or to modify appliance to pass through 'Accept-Ranges' and not coalesce responses for presigned S3 traffic. Support to validate after customer patch.

Follow-ups: Opened internal RFC with infra team to add a checksum-verify-and-retry loop in agent fetcher for presigned artifacts (NON-BREAKING change), and to add an alert when >5% checksum failures occur per region.
Ticket resolution criteria: Customer confirms stable artifact pulls for 48 hours post-change and schedules vendor upgrade or long-term config change. Marked In Progress until confirmed.
next_steps: 1) Customer to upgrade FastEdge or disable range-merge permanently for S3 presigned traffic (owner: NimbleRetail SRE).
2) Redwood to instrument artifact-fetcher with an optional single-range fallback and checksum-verified retry mode (owner: Diego / Infra team, PR linked above).
3) After customer change, run 48-hour validation job and close the ticket if no regressions observed (owner: Support/CS).
